html:
A kingdom of the Yue people in what is now Fujian, on China's southeast coast, from the late 4th century BCE until 110 BCE. The map shows it in 200 and 100 BCE.

Its kings claimed descent from Goujian, king of the old state of Yue, whose heirs fled south after Chu broke that kingdom. The Qin made the area a commandery, but after Qin fell the Yue leader Wuzhu helped the founder of the Han, and in 202 BCE he was recognised as king of Minyue. His capital was at Dongye, near modern Fuzhou.

Minyue fought its neighbours, including Nanyue and the smaller Eastern Ou. When it rebelled, Emperor Wu of Han sent armies by land and sea, and in 110 BCE the kingdom ended. Much of its people were moved north, between the Yangtze and Huai rivers. The name Min lives on as the short name of Fujian and of its Min Chinese dialects.
sum: A kingdom of the Yue people in what is now Fujian, on China's southeast coast, from the late 4th century BCE until 110 BCE. The map shows it in 200 and 100 BCE.
